chapter_theme: One song for the lord of Ezhukarai Nadu (எழுகரைநாடு): the poet asks to weep, sing the six-syllable names and become a servant in love night and day, and be given the stainless meaning.

986.reading: The poet asks that, gazing without guile, melting and praising, eyes full of tears and love growing ever greater night and day with no other distraction, singing 'Kumara, Muruga, six-lettered one, Saravana, who drank the milk of the Krittikas' with faltering speech, worshipping and weeping again and again, he become Murugan's servant and be given the wholly stainless meaning. The praise names Murugan who showed the supreme path, the son of Parvati and of Pasupati who fought Kama with his eye, the vel that set the sea afire and the seven hills roaring, and the lord who settled the gods in their land and rules the people of Ezhukarai Nadu.
986.nuance: The plea asks for the signs of bhakti themselves, tears, melting, faltering speech (மொழி குழறா), weeping (அழுதழுது), rather than for release from women or death, and only then for the meaning (மலாப் பொருள்). ஷடாக்ஷர names the six-syllable mantra of Murugan.

links.note: Thiruppugazh 986 asks for the signs of devotion themselves: melting (உருகியும்), eyes brimming (விழிபுனல் தேக்கிட), love growing night and day (இராப்பகல்), faltering speech and weeping again and again (அழுதழுது). Tirumanthiram 2980 reports the same state as already reached: அன்புள் உருகி அழுவன் அரற்றுவன், என்பும் உருக இராப்பகல் ஏத்துவன். The pairing shows the bhakti the song prays for is the state the Tirumanthiram names as the mark of those who have joined the Lord.

Kural 71 says no bolt can shut in love, since the small tears of the loving (ஆர்வலர் புன்கணீர்) proclaim it. Thiruppugazh 986 turns the tears into the thing prayed for, eyes brimming (விழிபுனல் தேக்கிட) with love growing ever more (அன்பு மேன்மேல்). The Kural treats tears as the sign of love; the song asks for the sign as the gift.
